Summary: In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 (PDB 1t1j) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (PDB 1f8y) were in different folds of the a/b class, so SCOP asserted no homology and not even fold-level similarity between them. In the current SCOPe release (2.08, stable; release date 2021-09-22, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16), PA1492 has been moved into the same fold and superfamily as 1f8y, so SCOPe now asserts probable common ancestry at the superfamily level, while keeping them in separate families. This matches the Andreeva et al. 2008 description of PA1492 as an example of a 'hypothetical protein' singleton fold being merged into an existing superfamily once a remote relationship was recognized.

Verified SCOPe 1.69 facts (queried separately):
- 1t1j: domains d1t1ja_ (sunid 106249) and d1t1jb_ (sunid 106250), sccs c.137.1.1. Lineage: class c (Alpha and beta proteins (a/b), sunid 51349) > fold c.137 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110459) > superfamily c.137.1 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110460) > family c.137.1.1 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110461) > protein 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110462) > species Pseudomonas aeruginosa (sunid 110463). This was a singleton fold/superfamily/family created for this structural genomics target.
- 1f8y: domains d1f8ya_ (sunid 31395) and d1f8yb_ (sunid 31396), sccs c.23.14.1. Lineage: class c > fold c.23 'Flavodoxin-like' (sunid 52171) > superfamily c.23.14 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52309) > family c.23.14.1 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52310) > protein 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52311) > species Lactobacillus leichmannii (sunid 52312).
- Relationship in 1.69: lowest shared node is the class (c). Different folds (c.137 vs c.23). SCOP 1.69 made no homology assertion and no fold-level structural-similarity assertion between them.

Verified SCOPe 2.08 facts:
- 1t1j: the PA1492 domains are now d1t1ja1 (sunid 106249, A:1-118) and d1t1jb1 (sunid 106250, B:1-118), sccs c.23.14.2. Lineage: class c > fold c.23 'Flavodoxin-like' (sunid 52171) > superfamily c.23.14, now renamed 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' (sunid 52309) > family c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110461) > protein (sunid 110462) > species Pseudomonas aeruginosa [TaxId: 287] (sunid 110463). The domain sunids (106249, 106250) and the family/protein/species sunids (110461-110463) were preserved across the move; the fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1 nodes (sunids 110459, 110460) no longer appear in the lineage. Annotation: 'Structural genomics target'. Homology section: homology implied by level, no warnings, no heterogeneity.
- 1t1j also now carries separate artifact domains d1t1ja2 (sunid 282689, A:0-0) and d1t1jb2 (sunid 282690, B:-6-0) in class l (Artifacts) > l.1.1.1 Tags > N-terminal Tags. These are expression-tag residues split off from the biological domain. SCOPe explicitly warns that class l artifacts are not homology evidence, so they play no role in the relationship to 1f8y.
- 1f8y: d1f8ya_ (sunid 31395) and d1f8yb_ (sunid 31396) remain c.23.14.1 in fold c.23 > superfamily c.23.14 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' > family c.23.14.1 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' > protein 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase' > species Lactobacillus leichmannii [TaxId: 28039]. Annotations: complexed with 5-methyl-2'-deoxypseudouridine (ligand 5md). Homology section: no warnings.
- Relationship in 2.08 (compare_scop_domains, d1t1ja1 vs d1f8ya_): relationship 'same_superfamily'; lowest shared node is superfamily c.23.14 (sunid 52309), N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like; no caveats present.

How the relationship changed, by level: class c was shared in both releases (no change). Fold: different in 1.69 (c.137 vs c.23), the same (c.23 Flavodoxin-like) in 2.08. Superfamily: different in 1.69, the same (c.23.14) in 2.08, i.e., SCOPe moved from no homology assertion to an assertion of probable common ancestry. Family: different in both releases (c.137.1.1 then; c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 now), so SCOPe still does not place them in the same family, which is the level implying clear sequence-detectable or otherwise strong evidence of close relationship. The superfamily name was also generalized from 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' to 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like', consistent with it now including a member of unknown function.

Limits: (1) The API shows that the classification changed and in which release range (between 1.69 and 2.08); it does not expose the intermediate release in which the merge occurred nor the curators' structural/sequence rationale. I did not verify that rationale from SCOPe data; attributing it to the Andreeva et al. 2008 discussion is based on the question's premise and general knowledge, not retrieved evidence. (2) Shared superfamily supports probable common ancestry, not identical biochemical function. PA1492 is still labelled 'Hypothetical protein' and 'Structural genomics target' in 2.08; the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase activity, catalytic residues, or substrate specificity of 1f8y should not be transferred to PA1492 on the basis of superfamily placement alone, and 1f8y should not be treated as an interchangeable structural or functional template for PA1492 without alignment- and active-site-level evidence. (3) Separate families mean SCOPe does not assert the closer, family-level relationship.
